unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9-LEVEL: B1.1 - THEME 5: LIFE IN THE HOUSE & NEIGHBOURHOOD

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students prepare a self-recording (visual, audio) at school/ at home, conducting an interview with classmates about their ''types of houses, rooms, furniture, and activities in the house'' and present it to the class and receive feedback on it. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: It is generally accepted that people who start to learn a new language bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning. For instance, this theme is based on the concept of ''the types of houses, rooms, furniture, and activities in the house'' and these students are expected to know what a house is, what a room is, what a piece of furniture is, and what an activity to do in the house is in their own language, as they are in year 9 (nine) of upper-secondary school. They are also aware that most people live in different types of houses with different rooms and furniture, and that they do different activities in their houses. Students can think about and express such facts and situations in their own language, but they may not know how to say them in a foreign language if they have not been covered at all or only partially covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language would prepare them to identify the same concepts later and help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information about the new concept and theme more easily in their foreign language, English. In terms of preparation for the current new theme, it is assumed that the students have learnt some basic vocabulary items for ''the types of houses, rooms, furniture, and activities in the house'' such as ''house, living room, bedroom, kitchen, sofa, bed, chair, to wash, to sleep, to eat etc.'' in previous themes or years. It is also assumed that they have learnt how to ask and answer questions to introduce houses, rooms, furniture, and activities such as ''How many rooms are there in your house? There are 3 rooms in our house. Is your house big? No, It’s/is small'' through grammatical structures that practise ''verb to be (am/is/are) in the Simple Present Tense in English from the previous themes or years. These vocabulary items and grammatical structures will be used as a base by revising and also extending them to learn the new or additional vocabulary and grammatical structures in the current theme by making the new grammar elements easier to learn.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is expected that students’ physical, cognitive, affective, social, and cultural factors are appropriate and suitable for learning about ''the types of houses, rooms, furniture, and activities in the house'' as a topic. Recalling and practising basic vocabulary for ''the types of houses, rooms, furniture, and activities in the house'' in English that they have learnt in the previous years would be helpful as a basis for moving on and learning the current content on the concept of ''the types of houses, rooms, furniture, and activities in the house''. Therefore, a quiz game can be played where each student can ask a simple question about the types of their houses, the rooms, furniture, and activities in their houses using the words s/he already knows (learnt in the previous years and revised at the beginning of the year) in pairs or in larger groups to revise all these vocabulary and grammatical structures from the previous themes or previous years by giving instructions in English as a preparation practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated to see how much they remember and how much they are able to understand, select and use the previously learnt vocabulary and grammar to build their competence in the current theme. It can be decided what to emphasise or practise in order to revise the previous knowledge and to facilitate the recognition, selection and use of target vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme.
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To describe rooms, furniture, and house activities in English through paired reading and question- asking activity by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Paired Jigsaw Reading - House Activities and Furniture The teacher prepares a text that describes different rooms, furniture, and activities that take place in various parts of the house. The text is divided into two sections, each focusing on different rooms and activities (e.g., the kitchen and the living room, or the bedroom and the garden). Students are paired up, and each student reads one section of the text independently. After reading, the students take turns asking each other questions about the rooms, furniture, or activities they didn’t read about. For example, Student A might ask, ''What activities take place in the living room?'' or ''What furniture is in the bedroom?'' This helps them complete their understanding of the entire text by filling in the missing information from their peer. At the end of the activity, each pair submits a completed worksheet that includes details about all the rooms, furniture, and activities covered in the text. The teacher evaluates how effectively students communicate and collaborate with their peers. S/he checks the correctness in answering questions and the completion of the worksheet for clarity, accuracy, and appropriate use of house- related vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students compare and talk about different visuals of the same room by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Paired Picture Comparison - Living Room Activities The teacher provides each pair of students with two different pictures of the same room (e.g., a living room). In one picture, there might be a father watching TV, while in the other, a mother might be reading a newspaper in the same room. Each student receives one picture and does not show it to their peer. The students take turns asking questions to discover what is happening in their peer’s picture. For example, Student A might ask, ''Is anyone sitting on the sofa?'' or ''What is the person in your picture doing?'' This way, they work together to fill in the missing information about their own pictures. Once the activity is complete, both pictures are displayed on the board, and the class compares them to see the similarities and differences between the two. The teacher and the class provide feedback on the meaning, accuracy and completeness of the descriptions, as well as the students’ use of vocabulary and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe different rooms, furniture, and activities in the house in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: House and Activity Pictionary In this activity, the teacher prepares small pieces of paper with vocabulary related to rooms, furniture, and activities in the house (e.g., bedroom, dining table, brushing teeth, ironing clothes), folds them, and places them in a box. The class is divided into teams, and one student from each team picks a piece of paper and must draw the word on the board without speaking. The other team members guess what is being drawn, and once they guess correctly, they must use the word in a sentence that describes an action at home (e.g., ''My sister is watching TV in the living room.''). The teacher awards points for correct guesses and accurately formed sentences, and the team with the highest score wins. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To describe different rooms, furniture, and activities in the house in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: House Vocabulary Bingo The teacher gives students a bingo card with rooms, furniture, and activities. S/he calls out the words, and students mark the words they hear on their cards. The first student to complete a bingo wins and forms sentences using the words from their bingo card and says it aloud. Then, the teacher evaluates the student’s sentences for meaning, accuracy, correct use of vocabulary, and grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
